clinical.citation: Bi-allelic PRMT9 loss-of-function variants cause a syndromic form of intellectual disability (PMID: 41260215)

variants.description: Single copy gain (duplication) of a region spanning the last exons of PRMT9 and TMEM184C (family Z, individual Z-II.1); exact coordinates not given in the excerpt
phenotypes: Individual-level phenotype not given in the excerpt. The cohort is described as having a neurodevelopmental disorder with global developmental delay, learning disabilities, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy and hypotonia.

clinical.diagnostic_reason: The copy gain was considered relevant to PRMT9 (a possible bi-allelic PRMT9 loss-of-function mechanism), not TMEM184C. No other pathogenic PRMT9 variant in trans was found by Sanger sequencing or WES, and whole-genome sequencing was performed. TMEM184C was only co-involved in the CNV, and no pathogenic role for TMEM184C is claimed.
